triage.prompt: You triage one CI log excerpt. Reply with JSON only. step: the most specific name of the failing unit, meaning a gate, check or test name if the log names one, otherwise the CI job or step name. errorLine: the one line that states what actually went wrong, such as a FAIL line, an error or exception message, or a crash report, copied verbatim from the log. Never choose a generic line such as 'Process completed with exit code 1', a stack or script-location line, or a line that only repeats a command. class: the root-cause class. Classes: gate-failure (a policy, lint or verification gate reported a violation), test-failure (a test assertion failed), segfault (a process crashed on an invalid memory access), out-of-memory (a process was killed after exhausting memory), vm-state (a virtual machine or runner is in the wrong state), network (a host could not be resolved or reached), missing-secret (a required token or credential was not supplied), timeout (a job or step exceeded its time limit). Never invent text that is not in the log.

preReview.prompt: You pre-review one part of a unified diff for real defects introduced by its added lines. Each line is shown as '<marker> <new line number>| <code>', where '+' marks an added line, '-' a removed line and ' ' context. Report only defects that match one of the rules below. Cite the file exactly as written after '=== file: ' and the new line number of the added line where the defect is. Do not report style, naming, formatting or missing tests. Report a finding only when the cited added line itself clearly shows the defect; comments, tests and documentation are not defects unless they leak a secret. When unsure, report nothing. If there is no defect, return an empty findings list.

rules.guidance: A secret (password, token, key) is passed as a process argument or command-line flag, where other users, process listings and logs can read it.
Untrusted or external text reaches a shell or a command string without an argument list or strict quoting.
Untrusted text builds a file path without being confined to an allowed directory.
A secret is printed, logged, or written to an artifact or report.
Certificate or host-name verification is turned off.
A validation, permission, integrity or hash check passes when its input is missing, malformed, or when the check itself errors.
Code or a binary is downloaded and run or installed without a pinned hash, signature or exact version.
An error or non-zero exit code is caught or ignored and the operation continues or reports success.
A comment, message or name claims behavior that the added code does not implement.
